stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +75.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $28.98 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 105 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 105 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-13.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-03) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
stories.excerpt: Attack method exposes flaws in OpenAI, Google safeguards against AI nudes.
stories.lead:
Safety researchers continue to warn that a large volume of AI-generated explicit content is spreading unchecked, while regulators do little to meaningfully stop it.

This non-consensual content is commonly shared in text and direct messages or stored in private clouds where it’s less likely to be detected or reported, a Google co-authored study of Internet users across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom found this July. That’s why the “most critical intervention point” remains at the source: the harmful AI tools used to make the fake sexual images, Google researchers concluded.

stories.title: They war-gamed dimming the Sun. It went even worse than you think.
stories.excerpt: Solar geoengineering simulation shows what happens when geopolitics takes over.
stories.lead:
When it comes to deciding the fate of the planet, Colleen Golja always thought science and reason would have a seat at the table. That was until one morning last September in London, when the climate researcher took part in the first in a series of war games. The goal: to prevent an uncontrolled global race to develop a technology aimed at cooling the planet but that comes with vast, unknown risks that could reshape life on Earth.

“I thought that would be such an easy thing. Like, we can all agree to do ethical research and make sure it’s for the better of all humans,” she told WIRED. “And boy, was I wrong.”

stories.title: Houthi missile hits Aramco building after Saudi-led coalition hits Yemen fuel depot
stories.excerpt: The Saudi energy ministry says the Houthi attack caused a "limited fire" at Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran.
stories.lead:
A missile launched by Yemen's Houthi movement hit a building owned by Saudi Arabia's state oil company Aramco in the eastern city of Dhahran overnight, after a Saudi-led coalition struck a fuel depot near the Yemeni capital, Sanaa.

The Saudi energy ministry said the Houthi attack caused a "limited fire" in an administrative building at Aramco's headquarters.

Saudi authorities reported that several missiles and drones were intercepted elsewhere, and that falling debris injured four people in the capital, Riyadh.

stories.title: Starlink restrictions affecting Ukraine's front line operations, Kyiv says
stories.excerpt: Elon Musk's system allows Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and effectively guide drones to Russian targets.
stories.lead:
Speed restrictions on the key Starlink communications network have disrupted Ukraine's battlefield "missions", President Volodymyr Zelensky's adviser has warned.

Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukrainian troops had not been informed about the speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company. A source in the Ukrainian defence ministry later confirmed this to the BBC.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies. SpaceX has not publicly commented.

stories.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
stories.excerpt: The White House publicly asked for U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday as she faced mounting accusations of improper conduct.
stories.lead:
WASHINGTON — The White House publicly asked for U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday as she faced mounting accusations of improper conduct, and she announced within two hours that she was quitting, ending days of talk and speculation about her professional fate. Guilfoyle insisted that she would "vigorously defend" herself.

President Donald Trump's administration had said earlier Tuesday it had asked Guilfoyle to leave her post after she faced severe criticism over allegations she engaged in improper and possibly illegal conduct before and during her tenure in Athens.

stories.excerpt: On three occasions in the past 24 hours, top IMF officials have praised UK plans to reduce its annual levels of borrowing.
stories.lead:
"Get your fiscal health in order," is a key message at the the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) annual meeting here in Thailand.

The IMF is worried about the debts of the world's biggest economies. It is doing its job as a watchdog, looking for and warning about financial vulnerabilities.

In the meantime, the finance ministers of former crisis countries are boasting about how little their borrowing costs have gone up, compared to the world's biggest economies, such as the US.

stories.title: 'It's definitely tight trying to budget on maternity leave'
stories.excerpt: An estimated 47,500 people in Sheffield are unable to make ends meet and pay their bills.
stories.lead:
Almost 50,000 households in Sheffield are struggling to make ends meet and cannot pay their bills, according to a new cost of living report by the council.

Described as having a "negative budget", these people are unable to afford the necessary costs even after all benefit entitlements have been claimed and their outgoings have been reduced to the bare essentials.

In the same week the report was published, a new food pantry opened in the Woodseats area of the city, offering low priced food for anyone struggling with the cost of living.

stories.lead:
Bronx, N.Y. – First the bad news. After scoring 16 goals in both of yesterday's matches, the fifth-ranked Fordham water polo squad didn't score 16 today. Now the good news. The Rams scored 17 times today, defeating George Washington University, 17-12, in an MAWPC match in the Messmore Aquatics Center.

With the win, Fordham improves to 15-1 overall, 6-0 in the MAWPC while George Washington falls to 10-8 overall, 1-2 in the conference.

Freshman Oktavian Veklyuk led a balanced Fordham scoring attack, scoring four times, while three other Rams; sophomores Alessandro Salipante and Diego Tresa, and freshman Karlo Dragosevic each netted a pair of goals.

stories.title: Sunderland hope to enjoy warmth in Portugal after 53 years away
stories.excerpt: Black Cats can reboot season against Torreense in Europa League in break from tough start to the Premier League There is a pleasing symmetry about Sunderland’s Europa League trip to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday night. The club’s last competitive venture on European soil, 53 years ago, was…
stories.lead:
There is a pleasing symmetry about Sunderland’s Europa League trip to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday night. The club’s last competitive venture on European soil, 53 years ago, was the second leg of a European Cup Winners’ Cup second-round tie against Sporting in Lisbon for the FA Cup holders, then in the Second Division.

In a striking parallel, second-tier Torreense prompted widespread surprise by beating Sporting in the Portuguese Cup final last season. The reward was a place in the Europa League’s initial phase and their chances of reaching next spring’s sudden-death rounds were boosted when they beat Lillestrom 2-1 in Norway last month.
